title: MUFG gets ACCC greenlight for proposed GROW acquisition
full_text:
MUFG Pension & Market Services (MPMS) has received approval from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) for its proposed acquisition of GROW, clearing a regulatory hurdle for the superannuation administration deal.
The ACCC’s phase 1 determination, issued on 6 October, found the acquisition was unlikely to substantially lessen competition in Australian superannuation administration services.
MPMS proposes to acquire 100 per cent of the shares in Grow Technology Services through its wholly owned subsidiary Australian Administration Services, under a scheme of arrangement.
Speaking to Super Review, a MUFG spokesperson welcomed the decision and outlined the remaining steps.
“MUFG Pension & Market Services acknowledges the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission’s (ACCC) determination that the proposed acquisition of GROW Inc. may be put into effect, following phase 1 clearance.”
“The ACCC’s determination represents an important and positive milestone in the proposed acquisition of GROW Inc, which remains subject to a number of further conditions and approvals, including approval from the Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) and the Japan Financial Services Agency (JFSA), as well as shareholder and Court approvals.
“We are pleased to have reached this stage and look forward to progressing the proposed acquisition through the remaining processes.”
The decision concerns two providers that have competed in superannuation fund administration tenders since GROW entered the market in 2020. MPMS, previously known as Link Group, is Australia’s largest provider of these services by funds under management.
In explaining its approval, the ACCC found GROW’s financial and operational challenges had weakened its ability to compete, despite customers valuing its technology, innovation and service.
“While Grow’s presence in the market is valued by customers who consider Grow’s technology, innovation and levels of customer service meet their SAS requirements, Grow’s competitive significance has been weakened by its financial position, operational challenges and uncertain future viability,” the determination stated.
The regulator considered GROW’s future without the acquisition uncertain, with possible outcomes including continuing under financial and operational constraints or exiting the market. It also considered the possibility of another buyer.
Market inquiries indicated larger superannuation funds generally did not consider GROW a competitive alternative because of concerns about its financial stability and experience. Several large funds questioned whether it had, or could obtain, the capital and scale needed to be a reliable provider.
The ACCC also found prolonged disruption to member services during HESTA’s transition from MPMS to GROW in June 2025 appeared to have weakened industry confidence in GROW.
Its determination noted APRA imposed additional licence conditions on HESTA in December 2025 over governance and risk management deficiencies that left the fund inadequately prepared to oversee and manage the transition.
The regulator nevertheless concluded MPMS would continue to face competition from alternative providers, identifying Apex and SS&C as established options with mature platforms and global capital funding.
Bravura was also identified as an alternative that could supply its technology platform directly or partner with other providers to deliver administration services.
Superannuation funds’ ability to bring some administration functions in-house would provide a further degree of constraint on MPMS increasing prices or reducing service quality, the ACCC found, although this option would not be commercially viable for every fund.
